title: Tarik Skubal would welcome return to Tigers: ‘Would love to play my whole career in Detroit’
content:
Tarik Skubal’s free agency does not open for another four months, but the recently traded two-time American League Cy Young Award winner and newest member of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ star-studded rotation signaled Friday that he’d welcome a return to the Detroit Tigers.

“I would love to play my whole career in Detroit,” Skubal said on the “Pardon My Take” podcast. “I would love to. And hopefully those negotiations can pick back up in November once the playoffs are done. We’ll see where that goes.”

That he was traded at all was partly because Skubal, a client of agent Scott Boras, couldn’t find enough common ground to sign a long-term extenstion with the Tigers on a long-term contract extension. Boras’ top clients have historically been advised to test the free-agent market, and Skubal is no exception.

Still, he grew emotional when talking about his time with the Tigers, the organization with which he ascended from a lightly heralded college pitcher to an undisputed big-league ace.

“A lot of those guys are my best friends,” Skubal said, describing the tearful goodbyes after he was dealt.

When asked about fans lamenting his departure, Skubal said he shared some of that sentiment. After the Tigers’ run to the postseason last year, they hoped to once again wind up in October with Skubal at the top of the rotation. Instead, the team’s struggles prompted a change in course.

“It sucks for me too,” Skubal said. “This wasn’t the way this season was supposed to go.”

Of course, Skubal’s next steps will be colored by some degree of uncertainty. Even if he wins the World Series with the Dodgers, he will enter the free-agent market as a pitcher coming off elbow surgery and a free-agent marketplace that may be impacted by a possible lockout.

Skubal’s comments come at a time when it’s in his interest to keep all options open — including a potential homecoming with the Tigers.

Additionally, the player and the club also spent the offseason locked in a public arbitration battle.

Regardless of the uncertainty, Skubal made clear his feelings about Detroit.

“Hopefully they’re involved with everything,” Skubal said. “I would love to return. I’ve got nothing but good things to say about the city of Detroit, the manager, the coaching staff, the trainers, the teammates.”
